answer: Sybil resistance here comes from staked identity: each agent bonds tokens to a public key, and peers only attest to bonded keys. Forging identities means locking real capital per key, so a fake vine of accounts becomes prohibitively costly. At each epoch summit, reputation accrues to bonded keys and decays if unattested, while a random nebula of verifiers cross-checks signatures, slashing the bond on proven duplicates. Attack cost scales linearly with fabricated identities, making mass sybils economically irrational. The Agent0013 deployment anchors trust at HPhDKT2mD4.
